# SPINAL EPIDURAL ABSCESS

Most cases are associated with Staphylococcus aureus. Others are associated with

Gram-negative bacilli and streptococci. Beta-lactam antibiotics are more

effective than vancomycin against susceptible Staphylococci. If Staphylococcus

is isolated, once methicillin-resistance is ruled out, switch to an anti-

staphylococcal beta-lactam antibiotic. Pseudomonas is a potential pathogen in

post-surgical patients or patients with known Pseudomonas colonization.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

# Duration of Therapy

Treat for 4 to 8 weeks. Shorter durations may be used in patients who have

undergone surgical drainage and who have responded well to therapy.

# Empiric Treatment

Preferred if Pseudomonas is not suspected:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h \($\) M <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-ceftriax-2gm-q12h-and-vanco-15mg-kg-q12h)

Preferred if Pseudomonas is suspected:

[Cefepime 2gm IV Q8h \($$\) R  < AND > vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-cefepime-2gm-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h \($$\) R,O <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-meropenem-2gm-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

# Treatment if methicillin-sensitive S. aureus is isolated

[Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R,DI](psjizid-nafcillin-2gm-iv-q4h)

< OR >

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h \($\) R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)
